Does the analysis recover a planted effect?

Source: R/plntfx.R
plntfx.Rd

Plants effects of known size in the real data and checks that the analysis finds them: the outcome is shuffled across rows, which removes whatever association it had with the treatment and the covariates while keeping its distribution, an effect eff is added to the treated (y* = shuffled y + eff d), and the analysis is run again, nrep times for each effect. An analysis that is biased, or whose intervals are too narrow, shows it here on data where the truth is known, a positive control in the sense of Lipsitch, Tchetgen Tchetgen and Cohen (2010).

Usage

plntfx(
  data,
  y,
  d,
  x = NULL,
  eff,
  nrep = 200,
  se = c("hc1", "iid"),
  level = 0.95,
  tol = NULL,
  seed = NULL
)

# S3 method for class 'plntfx'
print(x, ...)

Arguments

data

A data frame, one row per unit.

y

The name of the outcome column (numbers).

d

The name of the treatment column (numbers; it must vary).

x

NULL or the names of the covariate columns (numbers); for print(), an object of class plntfx.

eff

The effects to plant, in the outcome's units: finite numbers.

nrep

The shuffles per effect: a whole number from 2 to 1000000.

se

"hc1" or "iid".

level

The level of the intervals: one number strictly between 0 and 1.

tol

NULL (three Monte Carlo standard errors) or the largest |bias| accepted: one number from 0.

seed

NULL (drawn from R's generator, so set.seed() fixes it) or a whole number from 0 to 2147483647.

...

Not used by print().

Value

An object of class plntfx, a list: tab, a data frame with one row per effect (eff, mean, bias, sd, rmse, cover, rej, tol, ok); and nrep, se, level and seed.

Details

The analysis is the coefficient of d in the least squares fit of the outcome on an intercept, x and d, with a classical or HC1 standard error and Student's t interval at level, as falsctl() fits it. For each effect: mean and sd of the estimates, bias = mean - eff, rmse (about eff), cover (the share of intervals holding eff), rej (the share rejecting 0 at 1 - level), and ok, whether |bias| is at most tol. By default tol is three Monte Carlo standard errors of the mean, 3 sd / sqrt(nrep). One shuffle serves every effect, and the shuffles come from the package's generator.

References

Lipsitch, M., Tchetgen Tchetgen, E. and Cohen, T. (2010). Negative controls: a tool for detecting confounding and bias in observational studies. Epidemiology, 21(3), 383-388. doi:10.1097/EDE.0b013e3181d61eeb

Morris, T. P., White, I. R. and Crowther, M. J. (2019). Using simulation studies to evaluate statistical methods. Statistics in Medicine, 38(11), 2074-2102. doi:10.1002/sim.8086

Examples

set.seed(6)
d <- data.frame(age = runif(200, 18, 60), t = rbinom(200, 1, 0.4))
d$y <- 0.02 * d$age + rnorm(200)
plntfx(d, "y", "t", x = "age", eff = c(0, 0.25, 0.5), nrep = 200,
       seed = 1)
#> plntfx: 3 of 3 planted effect(s) recovered within tolerance over 200 shuffles
#>   eff      mean      bias     sd   rmse cover   rej     tol   ok
#>  0.00 -0.002595 -0.002595 0.1514 0.1511  0.93 0.070 0.03212 TRUE
#>  0.25  0.247405 -0.002595 0.1514 0.1511  0.93 0.395 0.03212 TRUE
#>  0.50  0.497405 -0.002595 0.1514 0.1511  0.93 0.920 0.03212 TRUE
